emergency.localNoteCL: Chile has no single number: 131 ambulance, 132 fire, 133 Carabineros (police). Save your local ones in "My contacts" too.
emergency.localNoteUY: In Uruguay 911 handles every emergency. Save your health provider's mobile emergency service in "My contacts" too.
emergency.myDataMissing: Set the relationship to "Me" in your medical record to have your details here (blood type, allergies, medication) and show them to whoever is helping you.
emergency.familyHint: Taken from the medical records, oldest first. Phone, relationship and whether they show here are changed in each person's record.
emergency.fichaContactsTitle: Doctors, vets and others from the records
emergency.familyNoPhone: No phone: add it in their medical record
emergency.noContacts: No contacts saved yet. Search for the nearest ones or add your own: doctor, vet, family.
emergency.name: Name
emergency.namePlaceholder: E.g.: Police station 3, Dr. Pérez, neighbor John
emergency.sourceNote: Source: {{source}}. It's worth confirming the phone by calling once.
emergency.osmOffline: Offline: showing the official data included in the app (fire stations nationwide; police and health in Buenos Aires Province).
emergency.osmOfflinePackage: Offline: showing the {{country}} data saved on the device (fire stations, police and health centers from OpenStreetMap).
emergency.packageMissing: The offline data for {{country}} has not been downloaded yet: it downloads automatically the first time there is a connection.
emergency.osmError: Couldn't reach OpenStreetMap (its public servers are sometimes overloaded): showing the official data included in the app.
emergency.needPlace: Choose a place: your location, a waypoint or coordinates.
emergency.nothingNear: Nothing found within that radius. Try a larger one.
emergency.nearbySources: Sources: fire stations from IGN and the National Council of Volunteer Firefighters; police stations and health facilities of Buenos Aires Province (open data, CC BY 4.0); and OpenStreetMap when online. Phones may be outdated: confirm them when you can.

location.intro: What to tell whoever comes to help: coordinates (always work) and landmarks that make sense without GPS.
location.waiting: Waiting for GPS… It's faster outdoors.

gpsError.denied: The app isn't allowed to use your location. Enable it in the browser permissions.
gpsError.timeout: GPS took too long. Try outdoors.

location.searching: Looking up address, nearby streets and roads…
location.offline: Offline the address can't be looked up: the coordinates are enough to find you.
location.lookupError: Couldn't look up the address. The coordinates still work.
location.sources: Address and streets: OpenStreetMap (Nominatim and Overpass), online only. They're approximate: coordinates are the most precise.

radio.mineEmpty: Save the frequencies you're given at a mountain hut, a park ranger station, a mountaineering club or your group. If you save their place, they're sorted by distance.
radio.freqNamePlaceholder: E.g.: Frey hut, Andean Club, my group
radio.tonePlaceholder: E.g.: tone 88.5 Hz, channel 3, DMR TG 7
radio.notesPlaceholder: E.g.: they listen 8 am to 8 pm; call "Frey hut, Frey hut"

repeaters.title: Repeaters
repeaters.empty: Import your area's repeaters from a file: they're saved on the device, work offline and are sorted by distance.
repeaters.simplex: Transmit on the same frequency (no offset, or not reported)
repeaters.toneNone: No tone reported: it may not use one, or the data is missing
repeaters.toneDigital: Digital mode: set with color code / talkgroup, not a tone

output.text: The frequency the repeater retransmits on: set it on your radio to listen.

input.text: The frequency the repeater listens on. Radios work it out if you set the offset.

offset.text: The difference between both: usually ±0.6 MHz on 2 m (VHF) and ±5 MHz on 70 cm (UHF). On the radio it's "shift" or "offset", with its + or − sign.

tone.text: A low tone your radio sends with your voice to "open" the repeater; without it you're ignored. On the radio it's "T", "Tone", "CTCSS" or "PL". DCS is an equivalent digital code.

mode.text: FM is the usual analog handheld mode. DMR, D-STAR or C4FM/Fusion are digital: they need a compatible radio and other settings (color code, talkgroup).

repeaters.importedNoPlace: {{count}} repeaters imported, but the town of {{missing}} wasn't found: they go last, without distance.
repeaters.importedApprox_one: {{count}} came without coordinates and was placed at the center of its town (approximate distance, with ≈).
repeaters.importedApprox_other: {{count}} came without coordinates and were placed at the center of their town (approximate distance, with ≈).
repeaters.importNone: No repeaters found in the file. Use a CSV, GPX or KML exported from RepeaterBook, or a CHIRP CSV.
repeaters.howTo: How to get them: sign up for free at repeaterbook.com, find Argentina (or your province), tap "Export" and download the file (CSV, GPX or KML). If it has no coordinates, each one is placed at the center of its town (Argentina). A CHIRP CSV from your radio club works too. You can import several: they're added together.
repeaters.attribution: RepeaterBook data: "Data courtesy of RepeaterBook.com", for personal use. Confirm frequency and tone with the club before transmitting; transmitting requires a license.

radio.nacionalHint: During a power or internet outage, a battery radio is how you hear what the authorities announce.
radio.nacionalNote: AM reaches farther (hundreds of km at night); FM sounds better but only near the station. Frequencies: Radio Nacional (via Wikipedia); check them with your radio.
radio.nacionalNoteUY: Public radio: Radio Uruguay (AM 1050 in Montevideo) and its FM repeater network in the interior. AM reaches farther at night; FM only nearby. Frequencies: Radiodifusión Nacional del Uruguay (via Wikipedia); check them with your radio.
radio.nacionalNoteCL: Chile has no national public radio: this shows the Radio Bío-Bío network (private, with stations in every region), which reports emergencies. SENAPRED official alerts also reach phones through the Emergency Alert System (SAE). Frequencies via Wikipedia; check them with your radio.
radio.packageMissing: The {{country}} stations come with the country's offline data: it downloads automatically the first time there is a connection.

marine.name: Marine · VHF channel 16
marine.desc: Distress at sea and on navigable rivers and lakes. Monitored by the Coast Guard and ships

air.name: Aviation · emergency
air.desc: Monitored by aircraft and control towers

radio.distressNote: Transmitting needs a radio for that band. Use them only when a life is truly at risk: a false call is a crime.
radio.hamText: Radio amateurs set up emergency networks when communications fail (for example, in the 2013 La Plata floods). Transmitting requires an ENACOM license; Radio Club Argentino and local clubs run the courses. Nearby repeaters will be added once your own server is set up.
radio.securityNote: Frequencies of the Gendarmerie, police, park rangers or other forces aren't included: they aren't public, many are encrypted, and intercepting them without authorization may be a crime.

maps.offline: Offline: downloaded areas are shown; elsewhere only the country outline.

camera.to3d: Switch to 3D (tilt the map with two fingers)
camera.toFollow: Make the map follow me and turn where I face

maps.zonesHint: Download the places that matter to you (your city, an evacuation route, a shelter) to have them offline, with terrain and contour lines.
maps.centerHint: The area is the orange circle: move the map to change its center.
maps.estimate: About {{tiles}} tiles, ~{{mb}} MB (approximate: depends on how much is mapped).
maps.tooBig: Too much for one download (the service allows up to 3,000 tiles or 50 MB): use a smaller radius or less detail.
maps.doneWithErrors: "{{name}}" was downloaded, but {{count}} tiles failed. Download it again on a good connection to complete it.
maps.cancelled: Download cancelled. What was already downloaded is kept for next time.
maps.noZones: You haven't downloaded any areas yet.
maps.notOnDevice: Not on this device (it came from a backup): download it again.
maps.confirmDelete: Delete the area "{{name}}"? Space not used by other areas is freed.
maps.usage: Space used by the app on this device: {{mb}} MB.
maps.attribution: Map: © OpenFreeMap, © OpenMapTiles, © OpenStreetMap contributors. Elevation: Terrain Tiles (AWS Open Data).

weatherMap.title: Weather map
weatherMap.offline: Offline: the map, volcanoes, your waypoints and the last downloaded earthquakes and weather are shown.
weatherMap.failed: Couldn't update: {{sources}}. Showing the latest available.

legend.satellite: GOES‑19 infrared satellite: colors mark very high, cold clouds — storm clouds (NASA, every 10 min, ~45 min delay)
legend.radar: Radar: observed rain (RainViewer). In Argentina it only covers the northeast
legend.earthquakes: Magnitude 2.5+ earthquakes in the last week (USGS): red, last day; orange, 3 days; yellow, the week
legend.volcanoes: Volcanoes active in the last 10,000 years (Smithsonian); orange, those that erupted since 1900
legend.fires: 🔥 Hotspots detected by satellite (VIIRS, NASA) in the last 24–48 h: red dots, with a flame per cluster
legend.hazards: Disaster alerts (GDACS, UN and European Commission): 🌀 cyclone or hurricane, 🌊 flood, 🏜️ drought, 🔥 wildfire, 🌋 eruption. Green, orange or red background by severity
legend.wind: Wind by area in {{unit}}; the arrow shows where it blows to

weatherMap.disclaimer: Indicative data from open sources (NASA, USGS, GDACS, RainViewer, Open-Meteo, Smithsonian). These are not official warnings: in an emergency follow your national weather service and civil protection.

error.offline: Offline: the forecast downloads when there's internet.
error.invalid-response: The weather service sent an unexpected response. Check the weather source in Settings.

weather.tapDay: Tap a day for details: hour by hour through the day after tomorrow, and by night, morning, afternoon and evening up to day 7.
weather.periodsHint: This far out the hourly forecast isn't reliable: it's summarized by parts of the day.
weather.noHours: No hourly data for this day.

legend.title: What each value means
legend.temp: Temperature · FL = feels like (wind or humidity)
legend.rain: Chance of rain and millimeters falling that hour
legend.wind: Wind in {{unit}}: the arrow points where it blows · g. = gusts
legend.cloud: Cloud cover: how much of the sky is covered
legend.visibility: Visibility: how far you can see (under 1 km is fog)
legend.storm: Storm risk: energy available in the atmosphere for strong storms to form
legend.freezing: Freezing level: height where temperature drops below 0 °C (above it freezes or snows)

weather.trendHint: Beyond a week the forecast is much less reliable: use it to see where the weather is heading, not for detailed planning.
weather.legendWind: wind and gusts in {{unit}}; the arrow points where it blows
weather.warningsNote: Warnings computed by the app from the forecast; they are not official alerts.
weather.source: Open-Meteo forecast for {{place}}. Saved on this device to view offline.

rainAlerts.title: Rain alerts
rainAlerts.here: Warn me if it's going to rain where I am
rainAlerts.noWaypoints: To get alerts for a saved place, turn them on in that waypoint's page.
rainAlerts.enableNotifications: To get the alert as a phone notification, enable notifications in Settings.
rainAlerts.whileOpen: For now it checks every 15 minutes while the app is open. With your own server, alerts will also arrive with the app closed (for "where I am" it uses the last known location: with the app closed the phone doesn't give GPS to the app).
rainAlerts.dry: No rain in the next 2 hours
rainAlerts.raining: It's raining: {{amount}} in the next 2 hours
rainAlerts.modelNote: Outside North America and Central Europe these 15-minute steps are estimated by splitting each hour's forecast (no high-resolution model or open radar): treat the timing as a rough guide, give or take an hour.
rainAlerts.body: {{mm}} mm expected in the next 2 hours.

place.label: Place
place.manualHint: Paste or type coordinates. To use them often, save them as a waypoint.

sky.needPlace: Choose a place to calculate sun and moon.

polar.day: The sun doesn't set all day
polar.night: The sun doesn't rise all day

sky.twilightHint: Civil: enough light to move without a flashlight. Nautical: the horizon is visible. Astronomical: full darkness.
sky.timesNote: Calculated offline for {{place}}. Times shown in this device's time zone.

recommendations.intro: Define your household and how much each member needs per day. The app calculates how much you'd need, how much you have and how many days it lasts. It only suggests: it doesn't change your minimum stock.
recommendations.noMembers: Add who depends on your supplies, in groups: "Adults" ×2, "Kids" ×1, "Dog" ×1.
recommendations.noRules: E.g.: drinking and cooking water, 4 L per person per day for 14 days. You set the values by your own criteria or the guides you follow.
recommendations.unitHint: Only items in the category with this same unit are added up.
recommendations.appliesHint: With none checked, it applies to the whole household.
recommendations.noMatchingItems: No item in the category uses "{{unit}}".

starmap.cameraHint: Raise your phone to the sky: you'll see the stars in that direction.
starmap.dragHint: No compass: drag to look around and use + and − to zoom.
starmap.domeCompassHint: Whole sky with the horizon at the edge. Hold the phone flat: the top is the direction it points to.
starmap.domeDragHint: Whole sky with the horizon at the edge. Drag to rotate it.
starmap.belowHorizon: {{name}} is below the horizon right now.
starmap.guideSouthHint: Extend the long axis of the Southern Cross about 4.5 times and cross it with the line from the middle of the Pointers (Alpha and Beta Centauri): that's the south celestial pole. Straight down to the horizon is South.
starmap.guideNorthHint: Extend the line through the two outer stars of the Big Dipper (Merak and Dubhe) about 5 times to reach Polaris. Straight down to the horizon is North.
starmap.layersHint: Turn off what you don't need for a cleaner sky. Constellation names and the degree scale show when pointing at the sky.
starmap.redOnOpen: Turn on red night mode when opening the star map

portable.isPortable: You're using the portable package (offline). It doesn't update itself: when there's a new version, download it and replace the folder's contents. Your data is kept.
portable.newVersion: A new portable package version is available: {{version}}
portable.howTo: Download it and replace the folder's contents; your data is kept.

inclinometer.surfaceHint: Lay the phone on the slope (or on a pole resting on it) along the fall line.
inclinometer.sightHint: From below or across, sight along the phone's top edge until it lines up with the slope. This measures without stepping on it.

legend.low: Low · under 25°: rarely releases, but an avalanche can run down from above.
legend.caution: Moderate · 25° to 30°: caution, close to the dangerous range.
legend.avalanche: High · 30° to 45°: where the vast majority of avalanches release.
legend.steep: High · over 45°: snow sluffs off often; it's still avalanche terrain.

inclinometer.disclaimer: This is the risk from the slope angle: actual danger also depends on the snowpack and weather. Approximate reading; it doesn't replace the avalanche forecast or training for snowy terrain.

compass.flat: Heading of the top of the phone.
compass.noDeclination: Without your location declination can't be corrected: the compass shows magnetic north.
compass.calibrate: If the heading jumps or looks wrong, calibrate by moving the phone in a figure 8, away from metal and magnets.

error.not-gpx: The file is not a GPX.
error.empty: The GPX has no track or points.

tracks.pointsHint: They come with the track and do not mix with your waypoints. You can go to one with the compass or copy it to your waypoints.
tracks.noPoints: This track has no named points.
tracks.confirmUncopy: "{{name}}" is in the route {{routes}}. If you remove it from your waypoints, the route goes on without that point. Remove it?
tracks.name: Name
tracks.confirmDelete: Delete track "{{name}}"? Points you copied to your waypoints stay.

follow.title: Following {{name}}
follow.reversed: In reverse: from the end to the start.
follow.off: You left the track: it is {{distance}} away, towards {{bearing}}
follow.arrived: You reached the end of the track
follow.timeHint: On foot without stops: 6 km/h over distance; in elevation, 300 m of climb or 600 m of descent per hour. The larger of the two counts, plus half of the other.
follow.map: Drawing of the track with your position

about.title: About
about.link: About, report a problem and contact
about.footer: VikArg {{version}} · About, report a problem and contact
about.description: Tools to be prepared: inventory, emergencies, navigation, weather and more. Works offline.
about.privacy: Your data stays encrypted on your device: it is not sent anywhere unless you decide to (backup, sharing with a family member or a report).
about.feedbackTitle: Report a problem or suggest an improvement
about.feedbackHint: Tell what happened (or what you would like) in as much detail as possible: what you were doing, what you expected and what happened.

placeholder.idea: E.g.: have the inventory warn when there is not enough water for 3 days.

about.includeInfo: Include the version and technical device data (nothing personal)
about.githubHint: GitHub needs an account (free). If you do not have one, send it by email.
about.noMailYet: Reporting on GitHub needs an account (free). If you do not have one, copy the message and send it however you like; sending from here is coming soon.
about.coffeeText: VikArg is free and ad-free. If it helps you and you want to support its development, you can buy me a coffee (cafecito).

guides.title: First aid
guides.disclaimer: Guide based on the first aid recommendations of the European Resuscitation Council, the Red Cross and the Argentine Ministry of Health. It does not replace a course: take a CPR and first aid course. When in doubt, call {{medical}}.

env.label: Where you are
env.cityHint: Help arrives in minutes: call right away and hold on until they arrive.
env.wildHint: Help may take hours: besides first aid, keep warm, find shelter and ask for rescue with your location.

detect.result: Nearest: {{what}}, {{km}} km in a straight line (about {{minutes}} min by car). Over {{limit}} min = wilderness: {{env}} selected. You can change it by hand; if you are on foot far from a road, choose wilderness.
detect.nothing: No help center found nearby: choose wilderness.
detect.noLocation: Could not get your location: choose manually.

protect.title: 1. Protect yourself.
protect.text: Make sure the scene is safe before approaching (traffic, fire, wires, water, rocks).

call.title: 2. Call.
call.text: Call {{medical}}. In the wilderness, ask for rescue and give your coordinates.

responds.title: 3. Do they respond?
responds.text: Tap their shoulders and speak loudly.

breathing.title: 4. Normal breathing?
breathing.text: If not breathing or only gasping: CPR now, 100 to 120 compressions per minute on the center of the chest.

bleeding.title: 5. Heavy bleeding?
bleeding.text: Press hard on the wound; on an arm or leg, if it does not stop, tourniquet.

position.title: 6. Keep them warm and still
position.text: unless in danger. If unresponsive but breathing, on their side (recovery position).

share.title: Share with a family member
share.linkHint: Give your medical records, contacts and documents to someone in your family: they're added to what they have, nothing is deleted.
share.intro: So your family has the same data. Receiving never deletes anything: what's missing is added and, if something differs, you choose which to keep. Relationship and "Me" don't travel, since they depend on who's looking.

include.medical: Medical records (with photos, doctors and vets)
include.inventory: Inventory (items, locations, quantities and expiry dates)

share.passwordHint: Pick a password only for this file (not yours) and tell it to your family member in person or by call, not through the same channel as the file.
share.passwordShort: The password must have at least {{min}} characters.
share.downloaded: File downloaded. Send it to your family member (WhatsApp, email, cable).
share.receiveHint: Pick the file your family member sent and type the password they told you. Before saving you'll see what gets added.

error.invalid-file: The file isn't a VikArg share or it's damaged.
error.newer-version: The file is from a newer app version: update first.

share.relationshipHint: They arrive without relationship: fill it in each record (e.g. the sender's son may be your brother).
share.samePersonAgain: {{name}} is the same person I already have
share.inventoryHint: What you send is added to your family member's inventory: if they have locations with the same name (e.g. "Pantry"), quantities go there. Mostly useful if you share the house.
share.inventory: Inventory: {{items}} new items, {{lots}} quantities (lots), {{locations}} locations and {{categories}} new categories.
share.neverDeletes: Nothing you already have is deleted.
share.applied: Done: {{profiles}} new records, {{updated}} completed, {{contacts}} contacts and {{documents}} new documents.

transfer.needServer: Sending with a code requires a VikArg server. Set it up in
transfer.sendHint: Uploads the encrypted backup to your server and gives you a single-use code. The server can't read its contents.
transfer.instructions: On the other device, scan the QR with the camera, or go to Backup › Restore › Code. Valid once, until {{expires}}.

error.not-found: The code doesn't exist, was already used or has expired.
error.too-many-attempts: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes.
error.too-large: The backup is larger than the server accepts.
error.failed: The server couldn't complete the transfer.
error.invalid-qr: That QR isn't a VikArg transfer.

backup.exportHint: Creates an encrypted .vikarg file with your whole inventory and photos. Opening it requires your current password or the recovery key.
backup.never: You haven't made a backup yet.
backup.downloaded: Backup downloaded. Keep it somewhere other than this device.
backup.importHint: Replaces all data on this device with the data in the file.
backup.invalidFile: This file is not a valid VikArg backup.
backup.newerVersion: This backup comes from a newer version of the app. Update it first.
backup.passwordAtExport: Password you had when you exported it
backup.wrongPassword: The password doesn't match this backup.
backup.replaceWarning: All current data on this device will be deleted and replaced with the backup. Your password becomes the backup's password.

recovery.title: Recovery key
recovery.intro: If you forget your password, this key is the only way to recover your data. It is shown only once.
recovery.warning: Write it down on paper or print it, and keep it somewhere safe. Without the password and this key, your data cannot be recovered.
recovery.confirm: I have stored it somewhere safe

unlock.title: Unlock
unlock.newPasswordIntro: You unlocked with your recovery key. Choose a new password.

settings.title: Settings
settings.saverHint: Pure black background: on OLED/AMOLED screens black pixels are off and the screen uses much less power (no change on LCD; lower the brightness there). Also: no animations, rain is checked every 60 min, GPS and sensors stop while the app isn't visible, and augmented reality starts with the camera off.
settings.duskPlace: Dusk is calculated for your area (approx. {{lat}}, {{lon}}).
settings.duskNoPlace: Your approximate location is needed to know when it gets dark.
settings.redScheduleHint: During that time the whole app turns red to keep your night vision. The dusk location is stored rounded (about 50 km) and unencrypted, because the theme also applies while the app is locked.
settings.connectionsHint: Optional. The app works the same without them.
settings.serverUrlHint: For notifications and transfers. Empty = no server.
settings.deviceHint: Features available on this hardware and browser.
settings.storageNotPersistent: The browser may clear it when space runs low
settings.backupOpen: Export, restore or move to another device
